subject: [PATCH] nfsd: add NFSD_CMD_FILEHANDLE_GET for root filehandle lookup

reviews.author: Chuck Lever
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted four technical issues: the selftest's proc_filehandle() function fails to parse the /proc reply due to a prefixing issue, the new binary is missing from .gitignore, the code silently clamps handle size to NFS3_FHSIZE instead of capping it at maxsize as claimed in the yaml doc and kernel-doc, and fh_proc_mount() leaves self->mnt behind when mount(2) fails after mkdir() succeeds.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Jeff, thanks for the patch. Review findings:

1. The selftest's proc_filehandle() cannot parse the /proc reply.
   write_filehandle() emits the handle via qword_addhex(), which
   prefixes the hex digits with "\x" (net/sunrpc/cache.c), so the
   first hexval() call fails and the function returns -EIO.

2. The new binary is missing from tools/testing/selftests/nfsd/
   .gitignore, unlike the four sibling programs listed there.

3. The yaml doc for maxsize and the kernel-doc claim the handle is
   capped at @maxsize, but the code silently clamps to NFS3_FHSIZE.
   A caller passing 128 gets a 64-byte handle with no error.

4. My sashiko instance here noted that fh_proc_mount() leaves
   self->mnt behind when mount(2) fails after mkdir() succeeds, so
   teardown's rmdir() of the tmpdir fails.

Can you send a v2 that addresses these issues?


-- 
Chuck Lever (Come to NFS bake-a-thon! https://nfsv4bat.org)

2026-10-20.patch_summary: This patch adds a new netlink command, NFSD_CMD_FILEHANDLE_GET, to the NFS server (nfsd) that allows clients to look up the root filehandle of an export for a specific client domain. The command takes three parameters: the client domain name, the path of the export, and the maximum size of the filehandle that can be accepted by the client. The patch also includes a kselftest to validate the new command's behavior and ensure it matches the existing /proc/fs/nfsd/filehandle transaction interface used by rpc.mountd. A companion patch for nfs-utils will be forthcoming.
